scope: Proposition 6.2 (Common point traces) of the manuscript “Removable Boundaries and Rigidity of Circle Domains” (preprints/Removable-Boundaries-and-Rigidity-of-Circle-Domains-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 071 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2793106e2bc200b8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Ω, Ω′ be circle domains containing infinity, and let f : Ω → Ω′ be a conformal equivalence with f(∞) = ∞. Suppose ∂Ω is conformally removable. Let C be the set of point components of b C \ Ω whose corresponding components in b C \ Ω′ are also points, and denote their positions by f∗(x), x ∈ C. For each e ∈ {1, i} and almost every line ℓ parallel to e, {πe(f∗(x)) : x ∈ C ∩ ℓ} = 0. Here and below | · | for a subset of a line denotes Lebesgue length.
